STAGE 1 — design constraint extraction (goal: pick a curvature mechanism that cannot repeat round_20261105_024519_485's failure mode).
Read: the round brief's hard constraints and the earlier-round evidence summary (holonomy-path-behaviour-rq collapsed: level2_distinct_prefixes=1, l3_collision=1.0, l3_refinement_gain_bits=0; five geometric repairs failed; scale-ratio explanation excluded; diagnosed cause = assignment reads a transported codeword while reconstruction reads the untransported one).
Observed: the residual pathologies to avoid are (a) two copies of the codebook / two charts, (b) whole-row positive scalar behaviour multipliers that cannot alter an argmin, (c) geometry names with no per-code geometric quantity, (d) artanh-type blowups.
Reasoning: the only admissible curvature positions are per-codeword, in-chart quantities that enter the SAME distance used by both argmin and reconstruction, with no coordinate transport. Already-used signals to avoid: context entropy ranking (BRad-RQ), demand volume (HYPVOLCAP), level-wise prefix-transition score (CURVCTRL-SID), holonomy transport, prefix ranking.
Open at this stage: which behaviour statistic and which in-chart curved distance to pair, and how to derive every constant without tuning.

STAGE 2 — mechanism choice and constant derivation.
Choice: FLOWCURV-RQ. Behaviour statistic = per-item directed NET FLOW imbalance phi_i = (in_i - out_i)/(in_i + out_i + 1) from TRAINING-split directed transitions (sink/source polarity, popularity-normalised, therefore not a volume like HYPVOLCAP and not an entropy like BRad). Aggregated per codeword per level by transition mass into phi-bar_{l,k}, standardised and clipped to [-1,1].
Curved operator: per-codeword Lorentz radial geodesic distance in the SAME latent chart, d = (1/sqrt(kappa)) * asinh(sqrt(kappa) * ||r - c||), kappa_{l,k} = rho_l^{-2} exp(+s-hat_{l,k}), curvature = -kappa_{l,k}, so a sink codeword (phi-bar>0) gets larger kappa, slower-growing distance and therefore a larger basin (capacity), while a source codeword gets a tight basin.
Why asinh and not artanh: monotone, non-expansive, finite for all u; no saturation blowup (this was the last round's killer). Euclidean limit recovered exactly as kappa -> 0, which is the geometry-off switch.
Constant derivation (no sweep): scale reference rho_l = running median of ||r_l|| measured on training batches during the first epoch (floored at 1e-3); exponent gain 1.0 (unit standardisation of s-hat, documented default); clip +/-1; kappa clamped to [0.1/rho_l^2, 10/rho_l^2]. sqrt(kappa)*u = u/rho_l * exp(.-s/2) is dimensionless at every level, so the warp is active at shallow and deep levels alike.
Consistency guarantee: exactly one parameter tensor C[L,K,D]; the argmin and the reconstruction term call the same d(); the residual is r_{l+1} = r_l - c_{l,k*} by plain subtraction (no transport, no second copy).

CHANGE: Replace the squared-Euclidean term of every RQ level by d_{l,k}(r) = kappa_{l,k}^{-1/2} asinh( kappa_{l,k}^{1/2} ||r - c_{l,k}|| ) with kappa_{l,k} = rho_l^{-2} exp(+s_hat_{l,k}), where s_hat is the standardised, clipped, transition-mass-weighted mean net-flow divergence of the items currently assigned to codeword (l,k); this single distance is used both in the argmin and in the quantization loss, and the residual handed to the next level is the plain difference r - c_{l,k*}.

Behaviour buffers (built once, before Stage 2, from the training split only):

  phi_i = (in_i - out_i) / (in_i + out_i + 1) in (-1,1)  (sink > 0, source < 0).
Geometry (per epoch refresh, everything detached from the graph):
  Given current codes k*(i,l): m_{l,k} = sum_{i:k*(i,l)=k} mass_i ; phi_bar_{l,k} = ( sum_{i:k*(i,l)=k} mass_i phi_i ) / (m_{l,k} + eps) ; phi_bar = 0 if m_{l,k} = 0.

  d_{l,k} = asinh( sqrt(kappa_{l,k}) * u_{l,k} ) / sqrt(kappa_{l,k})

q_l

IDEA: FLOWCURV-RQ
TITLE: Directed-flow per-codeword Lorentz curvature on one shared codebook: the same warped distance decides the RQ assignment and the RQ reconstruction
MOTIVATION: The Semantic IDs are only as good as the per-level partition, and the last formal round died on assignment collapse (level2_distinct_prefixes=1, l3_collision=1.0, l3_refinement_gain_bits=0) because residual geometry was broken. Underneath that collapse is a capacity question: a single RQ codebook of 256 codewords per level is forced to spend equal metric volume on behavioural sinks (items that many directed transitions land on) and behavioural sources (items that only emit transitions), so deep levels stop refining and the SID degenerates to a collision-extension token. FLOWCURV-RQ gives each codeword its own in-chart curvature driven by the direction (not the volume) of training-only transition flow, so sink codewords buy basin width and source codewords stay tight, without ever moving the codeword or transporting the residual.
NOVELTY: Curvature is not a level scalar (CURVCTRL-SID), not a codeword radius from demand volume (HYPVOLCAP/BRad-RQ), not a prefix ranking, not a Gromov budget, and not a transport/holonomy path. It is a per-codeword negative curvature kappa_{l,k} acting inside the SAME latent chart as the codeword, through a Lorentz radial geodesic distance whose vertex is the codeword itself; the behaviour input is a signed density-normalised flow divergence per item, so a codeword's geometry encodes whether it is a behavioural attractor or emitter rather than how popular it is. There is exactly one codeword tensor: assignment, residual and reconstruction all read the identical parameter rows, which is the structural defect the last round was killed by.
